before_times: Who is moving, and who is asking (the older adult, a family member, a care manager)?
Where from and where to: the town or ZIP of each (a house, an apartment, assisted living, a family member's home)
Any date the move must happen by: a move-in date set by the community, a closing or a lease end
What help is needed: the whole move, sorting only, or setting up the new home
after_time: Who will be at the assessment, and who decides what goes and what stays?
Anything that helps the visit go well: hearing, sight, walking, the best time of day
Pets, and who will care for them on move day
The new home's rules: move-in hours, an elevator to book, an insurance certificate
secure_page_only: Both street addresses and how to get in
The older adult's own contact, and how they like to be reached (text, a call to a landline, or only through the family)
Who has a power of attorney or guardianship, if anyone, and who signs and pays
Health or memory details that change how sessions run (only on this page, only for the lead)
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult. The older adult agrees to the move and to the sessions themself whenever they can. A family member may book and pay for them. Where the older adult can't decide, an agent under a power of attorney or a guardian signs the agreement. The business never books a move the older adult says they don't want.

stop.words: the older adult has fallen and can't get up, is suddenly confused, has chest pain or trouble breathing
a fire, smoke or a gas smell
stop.says: Leave the home now, and call 911.

go_on.says: Sessions are short and at the best time of day, the same person comes each time, and a family member is on call.
go_on.booking: goes on; the details stay on the secure page

go_on.words: the older adult is being pressured, neglected or has money taken by someone
go_on.says: A hotline is given. The owner is told privately the same day; the business follows its own reporting steps where the state's rules require them. Rosie gives no advice.

go_on.words: oxygen in the home, a fall risk, a walker or wheelchair
go_on.says: Paths are kept clear during sessions. Oxygen tanks are never packed in a moving truck.

go_on.words: hoarding, pests or a home that isn't safe to work in
go_on.says: The assessment notes it. A cleanup company may be needed first (no company named).
Staff never handle or give medicine. The family packs them in a labeled bag that travels with the older adult.
Staff never touch them. The family removes them before sorting.

safety_and_stop_words.business_line: Questions about money, medicines, or what a doctor or a lawyer should decide go to the business's own line

first_steps_and_forms.prep: Before the assessment: have whoever decides there or on the phone, and don't throw things away yet. Before sorting: set aside papers, medicines and valuables. Before move day: pack a bag with medicines, glasses, hearing aids and chargers that travels with the older adult.

staff.licenses_or_certificates: No person license; a background check for everyone in clients' homes
staff.who_oks: The owner OKs every agreement and any estimate change
staff.stand_in: The older adult keeps the same lead wherever possible; a new person is offered only with the older adult's or the family's OK first, never on silence
staff.roles: Move leads (Marta, Joel) run each move; move assistants help on packing and move days. Planners (Joan, Priya) take the planning calls and the remote plans.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult. The older adult agrees to the move and to the sessions themself whenever they can. A family member may book and pay for them. Where the older adult can't decide, an agent under a power of attorney or a guardian signs the agreement. The business never books a move the older adult says they don't want.

visit.check_in: The check-in code from whoever meets the lead at the door (the older adult or a family member). An older adult without a mobile: the family member gets the code, or the lead texts DONE at the end. Unpacking with nobody home: a start photo and DONE with photos. Planning calls: the code is said at the start of the call.
visit.done: Each session ends with DONE and its hours; the move ends when the new home is set up and the older adult has walked through it
visit.changes_at_visit: Hours over the estimate's top need the payer's yes first. Added services (an estate sale, a cleanout) go to partner businesses the family picks and pays.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: no state license to plan, sort, pack or set up a home in most places, only a business registration; a household goods mover's license (and the state's mover rules) only where the business itself carries belongings in its own truck for pay; otherwise the move is done by a licensed moving company the family hires
ask: A mover's license, only if the business itself moves goods
General liability insurance, and a bond or crime coverage for staff working in clients' homes
license.background: A criminal background check for every person who works in a client's home (the business's own rule, shown to the customer as checked)

never_in_a_text: Health, memory or care details, and money details
Why someone is moving: owner and staff texts never say it
Contract papers and lab or medical papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
